drafted_from: tool:github:facebookresearch-demucs's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs demucs.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use demucs on my computer to separate vocals from music: the file is song.mp3." It reads the row, installs demucs if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: demucs is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use demucs on song.mp3". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:facebookresearch-demucs"}.
2. It checks that python, ffmpeg are on your computer, and if demucs is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/facebookresearch/demucs.git ; python3 -m pip install -U demucs.
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input}: demucs --two-stems=vocals song.mp3
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: demucs on a 3 minute song file
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:facebookresearch-demucs runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got demucs in, the command line: demucs --two-stems=vocals song.mp3  (synthetic input: a 3 minute song file).
worked_examples.hands_back: demucs separates the song into two stems and writes them under separated/htdemucs/song/: vocals.wav (the singing) and no_vocals.wav (everything else).
